questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} & {e}^{2t} \\ 0 & -2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.
${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ $-{e}^{-4t}$ $\,,\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=\,\,$ $\frac{5}{4}$
{{field-1}} {{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} & {e}^{2t} \\ 0 & -2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{4t}\cdot (-2{e}^{2t})-0\cdot {e}^{2t}}[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{-{e}^{-6t}}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{2t} & -{e}^{2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{4t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-4t} & {e}^{-4t} \\ 0 & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]. \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-4t} & {e}^{-4t} \\ 0 & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-4t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-4t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int -{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -2{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-4t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{4t} & {e}^{2t} \\ 0 & -2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-4t} \\ {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{4} \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following system of differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

Using the method of variation of parameters, we wish to find a particular solution in the form ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t),$ where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system and $u(t)$ is a column vector of functions to be determined. A derivation of the formula for ${x}_{p}(t)$ is given below. 

$\text{L1}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$

$\text{L3}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)=AΦu(t)+f(t)$

$\text{L4}:\,$ ${Φ}^{′}=AΦ$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $Φ{u}^{′}(t)=f(t)$

$\text{L6}:\,$ ${u}^{′}(t)={Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)$

$\text{L7}:\,$ $u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${x}_{p}(t)=Φ\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t$

Select the correct options in the following reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}$ into the {{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L6}$ follows from line $\text{L5}$ by {{field-2}} both sides of the equation.

$\,$ Line $\text{L7}$ follows from line $\text{L6}$ by {{field-3}} both sides of the equation.
questions.worked_solution:
Let's examine each statement in turn.

- We first consider lines $\text{L1},$ $\text{L2},$ and $\text{L3}.$ Let's substitute ${x}_{p}(t)=Φu(t)$ from $\text{L1}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}(t)=Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t)$ from $\text{L2}$ into the initial system of ODEs:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =Ax(t)+f(t) \\ Φ{u}^{′}(t)+{Φ}^{′}u(t) & =AΦu(t)+f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\text{L3}$ is obtained by substituting $\text{L1}$ and $\text{L2}$ into $\text{initial system of ODEs}.$

- Next, we consider lines $\text{L5}$ and $\text{L6}.$ Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, its columns are linearly independent. So, $Φ$ is invertible. Therefore, $\text{L6}$ follows from $\text{L5}$ by $\text{pre-multiplying by }{Φ}^{-1}$ both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\cdot Φ{u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t) \\ ({Φ}^{-1}Φ)\cdot {u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t) \\ {u}^{′}(t) & ={Φ}^{-1}\cdot f(t)\end{aligned}
$$

- Finally, we consider lines $\text{L6}$ and $\text{L7}.$ To get $\text{L7},$ we are $\text{integrating}$ both sides of the equation in $\text{L6}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {u}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t & =\int {Φ}^{-1}(t)f(t)\,\text{d}t \\ u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}f(t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+\,\,\frac{1}{4}$ $8t-14$ .
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & 2{e}^{2t} \\ 2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}5t \\ 7t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{2t}-2{e}^{2t}\cdot 2{e}^{-t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -2{e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -2{e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int t{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =(3t)\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\cdot (3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =3t{e}^{t}-3{e}^{t} \\  & =3{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=1\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t & =(t)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{2})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{2})\cdot (1\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{t{e}^{-2t}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{4}(2t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & 2{e}^{2t} \\ 2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t}(t-1) \\ -\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{4}(2t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}12(t-1)-2(2t+1) \\ 24(t-1)-(2t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}8t-14 \\ 22t-25\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{t}-(-{e}^{t})\cdot 2{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & {e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & {e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=\frac{4}{3}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=\frac{4}{3}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{4}{3}t\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (\frac{4}{3}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}t{e}^{2t}-\frac{2}{3}\int {e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2}{3}t{e}^{2t}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t}(2t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=-\frac{8}{3}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-\frac{8}{3}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-{e}^{-t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t & =-\frac{8}{3}t\cdot (-{e}^{-t})-\int -{e}^{-t}\cdot (-\frac{8}{3}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}-\frac{8}{3}\int {e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}+\frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t}(t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t}(2t-1) \\ \frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t}(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}(2t-1)-8(t+1) \\ 2(2t-1)+8(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2t-3 \\ 4t+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

fields.input_html: 4t+2
